rationale: Interpretation of the AddNonvoter receipt 16e8004a30ec4b6da31b0914713fe698 (completed, exit_code 0) for the growth investigation. Parsed events: indices 37, 38 and 40 are the absent-server case called through AddNonvoter and 42, 43 and 45 the same call with the named server present; the neighbouring events in the same receipt are the AddVoter cases already interpreted. The predicate evaluated here is the counterevidence-sourced claim that the staged alternative keeps the cluster serving. It holds, which scopes the recorded defect to the AddVoter form of the call; the defect claim itself is unchanged and stays asserted. A fact records the scoping.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, naming a server that is not running yet through AddNonvoter keeps the cluster serving: the leader stays Leader with an unchanged term, the configuration entry commits, and client writes succeed; the same staging through AddVoter leaves the cluster leaderless and refusing writes. The difference is the suffrage the named server receives, since a non-voter is excluded from commitment and from the lease quorum while a voter is counted immediately.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, one-voter configuration grown by one member that is not running (unwired transport, no raft instance), in-memory transport, no faults; 1500 ms of 25 ms sampling plus a bounded client write, with the AddVoter and AddNonvoter forms run as separate cases in the same execution.

interpretations.rationale: Absent-server case through AddNonvoter (indices 37, 38, 40): the node stays Leader in all 59 samples of the window with its term unchanged at 2, the configuration entry still commits (commit index 2 to 3), and the bounded client write succeeds (no error, commit index 4), so adding the absent server as a non-voter leaves the single-voter cluster fully serving. The recovery phase reaches one leader with commit 6 without any repair being needed, and the named server ends as a follower. The control through AddNonvoter with the named server present (indices 42, 43, 45) behaves identically, which shows the difference between the two API forms is the suffrage the named server receives and not the availability of the server. Reading this against the AddVoter cases in the same receipt: the same staging, the same absent server, the same observation phases, and only the API form differs, producing a leaderless cluster in one case and an uninterrupted leader in the other. Predicate evaluated: the staged alternative (add a non-voter first and promote only when the server is ready) must keep the cluster serving while the named server is absent. It holds. This is a scoping and protective result: it confirms the recommendation recorded in the counterevidence of the earlier interpretation and shows that the defect is specific to the AddVoter form, which the API's own documentation still describes as adding a staging server that is promoted once ready. It does not change the defect, which stays asserted for the AddVoter conditions already recorded. Scope: protocol version 3, single-voter configuration grown by one member, in-memory transport, no faults, one process.

knowledge.assertion: The AddVoter step with an absent server commits and leaves the only node a leaderless Candidate that refuses writes until the named server appears.
In that state neither RemoveServer nor AddNonvoter for the absent server is accepted, and the node stays a Candidate.
The lease check and the election path read the latest configuration, so a voter that never answers removes the ability to keep or regain leadership.

counterevidence: This receipt is evidence for the safe alternative rather than for the defect; the defect's witnesses are the earlier AddVoter receipts.

The non-voter form leaves the named server outside the quorum, so it does not by itself make that server a voter; an operator still has to call AddVoter later, and that call has the same absent-server hazard if it is made before the server is running.
Both non-voter cases were observed for the same bounded windows as the AddVoter cases (1500 ms plus three seconds), so the comparison is like-for-like but bounded.
The recovery phases ended with the named server as a follower; its promotion was not part of this experiment.
limitations: One retained execution; the AddNonvoter and AddVoter variants are separate cluster instances built in the same harness rather than the same instance.
Only the single-voter configuration was exercised; the scoping statement is about that configuration and about the suffrage the named server receives.
The promotion step (AddVoter after the non-voter has caught up) was not exercised here, so the recommendation is supported for the staging step only.
In-memory transport, one process, default protocol version, deterministic conditions.
interpretations.joint_history: This receipt comes from the same harness lineage and staging as the other growth receipts, with the API form (AddVoter versus AddNonvoter) as the only difference between the cases; each case is an independent cluster instance built in the same execution and its sampling does not depend on the other cases.
interpretations.report_title: 分阶段加入非投票者不会影响单节点集群：与 AddVoter 直接加入投票者形成对照
interpretations.report_answer: 为验证此前作为反证记录的安全替代方案（先以 AddNonvoter 加入、待服务器就绪后再提升），本次保留执行 16e8004a30ec4b6da31b0914713fe698 表明：在命名服务器缺席的情况下改用 AddNonvoter，单节点集群在 1500 毫秒窗口的 59 次采样中始终保持 Leader、term 恒为 2、配置项仍提交（commit 2→3）、客户端写入成功（commit 4），随后无需任何修复即恢复到 commit 6；对照（同样调用 AddNonvoter，但服务器已在运行）行为一致。与同一执行中 AddVoter 的用例相比，仅 API 形式（目标获得投票权与否）不同，结果即从『无领导者且拒绝写入』变为『领导者持续服务』。结论：该缺陷专属于 AddVoter 形式——即库文档仍描述为『先加入 staging、待就绪再提升』的那条路径；安全路径在库中确实存在（先 AddNonvoter 保持非投票者身份，待其运行并追平后再 AddVoter 提升）。缺陷主张维持不变。
